details.verdict: The plans succeed under every scaling of the configured limits (x1000 range) and fail with none: they need SOME acceleration limit to exist and do not depend on its value; only the planned durations change.
details.conclusion: Planning requires that SOME acceleration limits exist and is insensitive to our values across three orders of magnitude (x1 to x0.001), which retires the A7 stop condition 'planning succeeds only because the acceleration limits we invented are generous'. It does NOT make the limits any less of a placeholder: they stay engineering defaults (velocity / 2 s; source engineering_default, status placeholder; ADR-009) with no payload, torque or controller analysis behind them.

answered_before_the_lift.1: (item 1 as it stood in P14, about the mast) the mast read as a thin spike. Its dimensions were those of an HFS6-60120 profile 14 mm shorter than the 1250 mm Alex specified on 28 Sep, so the appearance was an accurate thin extrusion and not a sizing defect; its orientation and its mass were defects (V01-F1, V01-F2), both now closed. The mast is gone: item 1 of the checklist now asks about the lift column and has no recorded answer

details.stays_warn_because: lift_mass_tl3_400 is null (no supplier mass for the fallback TL3 400 column), so one of the two columns the model offers cannot be built; V01 stays WARN until that datum is sourced, however the eight items land. The eight below are measured on dold_v4_350 only

findings.found: the mast profile was probably rotated 90 degrees: mast_section [0.060, 0.120] put 60 mm fore-aft and 120 mm lateral; option B (P-03 rev18.9 item 18) orients the same HFS6-60120 cross-section (its 340 mm arm profile, not a full-height mast) 120 mm fore-aft and 60 mm lateral, the stiff direction against the arms' forward cantilever. The value was right. Its axis assignment was only a prose note in the datum ('orientation unconfirmed') and no test asserted it
findings.outcome: confirmed correct by the design owner (Alex, 12 Oct 2026: 'thanks for catching the profile orientation, that's exactly the kind of check we need'); the 90 degree rotation was real
findings.resolved_by: the mast and mast_section are deleted (P15); the rule it proposed is implemented: a dimension list declares axis_convention and T12 asserts the assignment against the expansion

findings.found: mast_mass was 3.0 kg (placeholder) for 1.2365 m of HFS6-60120: about 337 kg/m3 over the bounding box, low by roughly 2.5 to 4 times for an aluminium extrusion (an estimate, not a datasheet figure). Labelled placeholder, so nothing lied, but the placeholder was implausible and nothing checked plausibility
findings.outcome: closed by the supplier catalogue figure: the lift is a DOLD Hexalift V4 350 of 11.7 kg (rev19.0, 12 Oct 2026). The estimate was 7.5 to 12 kg; the catalogue value is at the top of that bracket
findings.resolved_by: mast_mass is deleted with the mast; lift_mass_dold_v4_350 carries 11.7 kg (provisional: a catalogue figure, not weighed); the rule it proposed is implemented: a mass datum of ours declares a density_band and T10 checks it

limitations: `simulation` names the evidence class: every result here is how the model behaves in Gazebo Harmonic or on mock_components, planned by MoveIt 2.12.4 under OpenAMRobot's own declared limits. Every claim reads 'plans and executes in simulation under declared OpenAMRobot limits'; nothing here is a validated limit, a payload, a torque, or a statement about a physical robot

the acceleration limits are engineering defaults (source: engineering_default, status: placeholder; rule: velocity / 2 s) written because upstream declares none (openamrobot-manipulation#10, ADR-009); M06 shows the plans need SOME limit and do not depend on its value

the lift is not under ros2_control and has no authority to be commanded (option B: effort 0, velocity 0): its state is the operating point of a run (the mock stub's lift_position in M01; joint_state_publisher's default zero in Gazebo, not read from the physics), and MoveIt plans the arms from it. The three lift stops are calibration IDs, not configuration IDs

the lift column has no collision geometry (its lateral extent is not sourced): the arms can plan through the column body, and arm_profile_link, option B's 340 mm box, is the one collision body of the upper structure
`park` is a placeholder copy of upstream's `home`, until the safe-pose definition lands under the manipulation action contract

the gripper controller is still the deprecated position_controllers/GripperActionController serving GripperCommand (option 1 of ADR-009 point 4): this report does not choose between the three gripper interfaces (manipulation#11)

G02 and M02 pass the Bullet-Featherstone engine explicitly; sim.launch.py defaults to DART, the engine platform-sw tuned the base on, on which a closed gripper pose does not close. The base's contact behaviour was compared on neither engine
the arms' position interface in gz_ros2_control is a velocity servo, so a final error under 0.01 rad in M02 says nothing about the real arm's controller, gains, compliance or latency

MoveIt 2.12.4 refuses a start state any amount outside a joint limit ('Joint ... from the starting state is outside bounds by'), and a simulated joint resting on its limit (openarm_*_joint4 = 0, the home pose) reads back a hair past it. The joint state move_group plans from is therefore clamped to the limit by joint_state_clamp.py, by at most its epsilon, and only that topic: no limit was widened and no pose moved. The clamp's counters are in M01/M02 (clamp_totals) and a reading beyond the epsilon is passed through, never clamped
move_group exits with SIGSEGV when it is stopped (MoveIt 2.12.4); the checks allow that code for that one process and no other

the arms cannot reach the platform's base body: M04's refused goal is inside arm_profile_link's volume, the nearest structure volume a left gripper can be put in; the arms are 62 mm apart at their bases (option B's y = +-0.031) and the left gripper reaches the right arm's own links in some random states, which is a reach fact for A4

the collision matrix is DERIVED, not sampled (scripts/derive_acm.py): a pair is disabled only if upstream declares it, it is a structural neighbour (Adjacent), or no movable joint lies between its links and it is clear in the one evaluation that settles every configuration (ConstantTransform); every other pair is enabled. The Setup Assistant's sampler, which has no seed and gave a different matrix on every run, is no longer used. The checked-in SRDF is the contract and M03 validates that file

M03's sampled part is information about the ENABLED pairs, never a reason: sampling falsifies and does not certify. It lists the enabled pairs that collide in random states and how often (for A4); nothing in the matrix rests on it

V01 is WARN. P14's look at the mast found two defects (V01-F1 confirmed correct by the design owner, V01-F2 closed by the 11.7 kg catalogue figure), both resolved by the lift. P16 measured the eight items of the lift model (evidence/v01/): none reads outside its expected value, and two sub-questions that need eyes are marked cannot_measure. It stays WARN because lift_mass_tl3_400 is null (no supplier mass for the fallback TL3 400 column), so one of the two columns the model offers cannot be built; V01 stays WARN until that datum is sourced, however the eight items land. The eight below are measured on dold_v4_350 only. This report launches nothing for V01 and records no inspection of its own
no physical evidence; simulation only. This report is not a statement about hardware
